description:
Ylang Ylang (Cananga odorata) is a plant used to make a popular essential oil. This essential oil is highly toxic to cats and should never be used on or around them. Cats cannot properly break down compounds in the oil, such as linalool and benzyl acetate, because their livers lack a specific enzyme.

Exposure can happen through inhalation from a diffuser, skin contact, or a cat licking the oil. The toxic compounds build up in the cat's body, leading to nervous system problems like stumbling and seizures, as well as severe liver damage. Because the oil is so concentrated, even a small amount can be dangerous.

Symptoms of poisoning include drooling, vomiting, appearing drunk or unsteady, tremors, and breathing trouble. If you suspect your cat has been exposed to Ylang Ylang oil in any form, it is a medical emergency. Please contact a veterinarian or an emergency animal hospital immediately.
name: Ylang Ylang
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: germacrene, benzyl acetate, methyl benzoate, and other volatile sesquiterpene and ester compounds in the essential oil
Mechanism: cats lack the hepatic glucuronidase needed to metabolise these compounds efficiently; accumulation causes GI and CNS effects
Symptoms: vomiting, drooling, weakness, unsteady gait (ataxia), difficulty breathing; inhalation may cause respiratory irritation
Essential oil diffusers in closed rooms are a significant risk even without direct contact
Do not apply ylang ylang oil to or near cats; use diffusers only in well-ventilated areas the cat cannot access

symptoms.name: Walking as if they are drunk (ataxia)
Difficulty breathing or breathing with the mouth open
Sore, red skin, and chemical burns
Liver failure and serious organ damage
